gc_remedy.name: sitecustomize.py
gc_remedy.what: on SIGRTMIN+1 (sent by the serve script before any traffic): gc.collect() then gc.freeze() (reason warmup); then every 30 s a background thread repeats collect-then-freeze (reason periodic), so full collections never rescan the about 66M warmup jaxpr objects the server keeps; a light gc.callbacks log of gen-2 collections; gc.get_freeze_count() (O(n)) only once, at the warmup freeze
gc_remedy.why: pf1/pf2: full Python gen-2 collections over the retained warmup heap took about 13.3 s with the GIL held (the request loop stopped), every ~100-200 requests; each cost 4-5 decisions to timeouts (the r4a3 screen had the same at about 10 s, about every 5,000 requests); the real fix (the pricer keeping traced jaxprs) is a tree change for after r5a

gc_r1.note: compare.json holds only aggregate counts, so identical outcomes give identical bytes (as cert12-r3, gc-r1 and gc-r2 do); ran the earlier sitecustomize 69aa15c5... (logging only: the O(n) freeze count in the callback), which does not affect results; against the binding cert12-r3 (no remedy, its own fresh cache) every priced decision differed by at most |dQ| 1.76e-7 with 0 actions, statuses or refusals changed: separate autotuning on different GPUs, proven by gc_r2
gc_r1.what: the binding harness and 15 cells, ON vs OFF, the remedy active in both (fresh cache)

gc_r2.result: IDENTICAL; against cert12-r3 (no remedy): 0 differences ON vs ON and OFF vs OFF on all 495 priced decisions, the same 31 refused

identity.scope: The gate-12 claim is bitwise identity within one cache. ON and OFF share the cache by design. Cross-run differences at autotuning level are outside that claim and do not touch the certificate.
